order: say what happened and where you are
stay on the line until they say goodbye
safety: only for a real emergency: never to try it
an address is said out loud, never typed into a game

little.twist: The helper on the phone asks one more question: which helpers you need.
little.can_now: check it is safe, call {number} and say what happened and where they are

steps.say: Oh no! Bobo the buddy slipped and fell. Let's practise how to help. This is practice. A real first aid course teaches more.
First, look around. Is it safe to go near Bobo?

choices.why: Look again: nothing here can hurt you. It is safe to help.

steps.done: You looked first. Checking it is safe keeps you safe too.

steps.say: Touch Bobo's shoulder and ask: are you all right?
steps.done: Bobo says: ouch, my leg! Bobo is awake and talking.

steps.say: Now we call for help. Pick up the phone.
steps.done: Good. Now press the numbers.

steps.say: Press {number}: {number_words}.
steps.done: You called {number}. A calm helper answers.

steps.say: The helper asks: what happened?

choices.text: My friend fell and hurt a leg

steps.miss: Tell the helper what is wrong, so they send the right help.
steps.done: Yes: you said what happened.

steps.say: The helper asks: where are you?

choices.text: My address (I learn it with my grown-up)

choices.why: Stay on the phone. Say your address, or what you can see near you.
Say where you really are: your address, or what you can see.

steps.done: Yes! Learn your address with your grown-up and say it out loud. Never type it into a game.

steps.say: The helper asks: which helpers do you need?

choices.why: There is no fire. An ambulance helps someone who is hurt.
Nobody is in danger from a person. An ambulance helps someone who is hurt.

steps.done: An ambulance brings help for someone who is hurt.

steps.say: The helper asks: is your friend awake and talking?

choices.why: Bobo talked to you, so Bobo is awake.

steps.done: You noticed. That helps the helpers.

steps.say: The helper says: stay with your friend, help is on its way. Keep the phone on until they say goodbye.
Stay with Bobo. Hold Bobo's hand until help comes.
steps.done: Help is here! You stayed calm and kind.

steps.say: You did it! You called for help and stayed with your friend. In real life, grown-ups help too.

check.say: Someone is hurt. What do you do first?
Which number do you call for help?
The helper asks: where are you? What do you say?

name_it.title: Call for help
lines: Say what happened and where you are.
Stay with them. Help is coming.
name_it.source: The IFRC first aid guidelines (2020) and the ERC's Kids Save Lives

little.try_real: With a grown-up: find the phone at home and show how you would call {number} (only pretend: never call it to try). Learn your address and say it out loud together.

sources.fact: Check that it is safe for you before helping (danger first); then call for help and stay with the person.
sources.source: IFRC International First Aid, Resuscitation and Education Guidelines 2020

sources.fact: Children can learn to recognise an emergency and call for help (check, call); the WHO-endorsed Kids Save Lives statement.
sources.source: European Resuscitation Council, Kids Save Lives

sources.fact: 112 is Georgia's single emergency number (since 2012) and the European emergency number; the caller says what happened and where, answers the questions and stays on the line.
sources.source: Georgia's 112 service; the European Commission's 112 page

sources.fact: The European emergency number 112 works free in every EU country.

middle.skill: Cuts, burns and the recovery position
middle.twist: Bobo has a second little cut, and you choose what is right for a burn.
middle.can_now: press a cut with a clean cloth, cool a burn for 20 minutes and put someone in the recovery position

steps.say: Bobo has a small cut on one arm and a sore burn on one paw. Let's practise first aid. This is practice. A real first aid course teaches more.
First, clean hands. Put on the gloves.
steps.done: Gloves keep germs away from the cut.

steps.say: Take a clean cloth.
steps.done: Got it.

steps.say: Press the cloth on the cut, firmly. Keep pressing.
steps.done: Pressing on a cut helps it stop. Well done.

steps.say: There is a second little cut on the other arm. Press on that one too.
steps.done: Both cuts pressed.

steps.say: Now cover it with a plaster.
steps.done: All clean and covered.

steps.say: Now the burn. Turn on the cool water.
steps.done: Cool, running water.

steps.say: Hold Bobo's paw under the cool running water.
steps.done: That's it.

steps.label: 20 minutes
steps.say: A burn needs cool running water for 20 minutes. Let's speed up the clock.
steps.done: 20 minutes of cool water. That is how long a burn needs.

steps.say: Which one is right for a burn?

choices.why: Ice can hurt the skin more. Use cool running water.
Butter keeps the heat in. Never put it on a burn.

steps.done: Cool running water. Never ice, butter or cream.

steps.say: Cover the burn loosely with cling film. And always tell a grown-up about a burn.
steps.done: Covered and told. Good first aid.

steps.say: Now let's pretend Bobo is breathing but won't wake up. We practise the recovery position: it keeps the breathing easy.
Move Bobo's arm nearest you out, like the letter L.
steps.done: Arm out.

steps.say: Put Bobo's other hand against the cheek.
steps.done: Hand by the cheek.

steps.say: Bend Bobo's far knee up.
steps.done: Knee up.

steps.say: Pull the knee towards you, and Bobo rolls onto the side.
steps.done: Bobo is on the side.

steps.say: Tilt the head back a little, so the air gets in easily.
steps.done: That's the recovery position. Breathing is easy now.

steps.say: What do you do now?

choices.why: Stay with Bobo and call {number}: help is on its way.

choices.text: Wake Bobo with a loud toy
choices.why: Let Bobo rest on the side, and call {number}.

steps.done: Call {number} and stay. Help is on its way.

steps.say: Brilliant first aid! You pressed a cut, cooled a burn and made the recovery position. In real life, grown-ups help too.

check.say: A cut. What do you do first?

choices.text: Press on it with a clean cloth

check.say: How long do you cool a burn?
Someone is breathing but won't wake up. How do you lay them?

choices.text: On their side: the recovery position

check.say: After first aid for a burn, who do you tell?

name_it.title: First aid for cuts and burns
lines: A cut: press on it with a clean cloth.
A burn: cool running water for 20 minutes.
Cover a burn loosely with cling film, and tell a grown-up.
Breathing but won't wake up: the recovery position, then call {number}.
name_it.source: The IFRC first aid guidelines (2020) and the ERC first aid guidelines (2021)

middle.try_real: With a grown-up: find the first aid kit at home. Show your grown-up how you press a cut with a clean cloth, and the recovery position (take turns lying down!).

sources.fact: Bleeding: press directly on the wound with a clean cloth or dressing; wear gloves or clean hands when you can.
sources.source: IFRC International First Aid, Resuscitation and Education Guidelines 2020

sources.fact: Burns: cool with cool running water for at least 20 minutes; never ice, butter or creams; cover loosely with cling film.
sources.source: European Resuscitation Council Guidelines 2021: First aid (Zideman et al.)

sources.fact: Burns: cool under cool running water for 20 minutes, cover with cling film, get medical help for a child's burn.
The recovery position for someone who does not respond but breathes normally: on the side, the head tilted back, the airway open.
sources.source: European Resuscitation Council Guidelines 2021: Basic Life Support (Olasveengen et al.)

big.twist: A defibrillator arrives, and the beat must be steadier.
big.can_now: call {number}, push on the chest at 100 to 120 a minute and help someone who is choking

steps.say: Meet Max, the training dummy. Today: hands-only CPR, and help for choking. This is practice. A real first aid course teaches more.
Max is lying on the floor. What do you do first?

choices.text: Check it is safe to go near

choices.why: Danger first: make sure it is safe for you.
Max needs your help. Check it is safe, then help.

steps.done: Safe. Now check Max.

steps.say: Touch both shoulders and ask loudly: are you all right?
steps.done: No answer. Max does not respond.

steps.say: Tilt the head back. Look, listen and feel for normal breathing, for up to 10 seconds.
steps.done: Max is not breathing normally.

steps.say: No response and not breathing normally. What now?

choices.text: Call {number}, then push on the chest

choices.why: Every minute counts. Call {number} and start pushing.
The recovery position is for someone who IS breathing normally.

steps.done: Call, then push.

steps.say: Call {number}. Put the phone on speaker, so your hands are free.
steps.done: The helper on the phone helps you. If someone is near, they fetch a defibrillator (an AED).

steps.say: Kneel beside Max. The heel of one hand on the middle of the chest, the other hand on top.
steps.done: Hands in place. Arms straight.

steps.say: Push hard and fast, to the beat: 100 to 120 times a minute. Let the chest come back up each time.
steps.done: That's the beat! Keep going until help comes or the defibrillator is ready.

steps.say: Push hard and fast, to the beat: 100 to 120 times a minute. Keep it steady this time.
steps.done: A steady beat! Keep going until help comes.

steps.say: A helper brings a defibrillator (an AED). What do you do?

choices.text: Switch it on and do what its voice says

choices.why: An AED talks you through it. Switch it on and follow it.

steps.done: The AED's voice tells you every step. Keep pushing when it says so.

steps.say: Pushing is hard work. If another helper is there, swap about every 2 minutes.
Now choking. Lulu the buddy is coughing: some food went down the wrong way.
Lulu can still cough. What do you do?

choices.why: While someone can cough, coughing works best. Back blows come if coughing stops working.
A drink can make it worse. Coughing is best.

steps.done: Coughing is the best way out.

steps.say: Now Lulu can't cough or breathe. Give up to 5 back blows: lean Lulu forward, then firm blows between the shoulder blades.
Five back blows, between the shoulder blades.
steps.done: Five back blows. Still stuck.

steps.say: Still stuck? Up to 5 tummy thrusts: stand behind, a fist just above the belly button, pull in and up.
Five tummy thrusts: in and up.
steps.done: Out it comes! Lulu can breathe.

steps.say: It came out. What now?

choices.text: Tell a grown-up: Lulu should see a doctor

choices.why: After tummy thrusts, a doctor should check them.

steps.done: A doctor checks anyone who had tummy thrusts.

steps.say: You did it: CPR to the beat and help for choking. If it doesn't come out: call {number}, and keep going, 5 back blows, 5 tummy thrusts. In real life, grown-ups help too.

check.say: Someone collapsed and is not breathing normally. What first?

choices.text: Call {number}, then push on the chest

check.say: Someone is choking but can cough. You...
Choking and can't cough or breathe. What comes first?

name_it.title: Hands-only CPR
lines: Check: no response and not breathing normally.
Push hard and fast in the middle of the chest, 100 to 120 a minute.
Choking: cough; then 5 back blows; then 5 tummy thrusts.
name_it.source: The ERC guidelines (2021) and the IFRC first aid guidelines (2020)

big.try_real: With a grown-up: find the nearest defibrillator (AED): at school, a shop or a station. Show your grown-up the CPR beat on a cushion, and ask about a real first aid course.

sources.fact: Hands-only CPR: compressions in the centre of the chest at 100-120 a minute, 5-6 cm deep, letting the chest come back up; call the emergency number on speaker; look, listen and feel for normal breathing for no more than 10 seconds; swap rescuers about every 2 minutes; use an AED as soon as it arrives.
sources.source: European Resuscitation Council Guidelines 2021: Basic Life Support (Olasveengen et al.)

sources.fact: Choking: encourage coughing; if coughing stops working, up to 5 back blows, then up to 5 abdominal thrusts; call the emergency number if it does not clear; anyone given abdominal thrusts should see a doctor.
sources.source: European Resuscitation Council Guidelines 2021: Basic Life Support (Olasveengen et al.)

sources.fact: CPR training for schoolchildren from about 12: check, call, compress.
sources.source: European Resuscitation Council, Kids Save Lives (endorsed by the WHO)

sources.fact: First aid for choking and cardiac arrest by lay people.
sources.source: IFRC International First Aid, Resuscitation and Education Guidelines 2020
